classification.difficultyReason: Translate an undirected weighted graph into a symmetric table, total specified walks, and identify an alternative route whose time is less than the given journey.

inlines.text: The network diagram below models forest walkways connecting a bridge (B), waterfall (W), a big tree (T) and a fern gully (F). Walkers enter the forest through gate 1 (G1) or gate 2 (G2).
The edge weights represent time taken to walk directly between these places.

spec.description: Six-vertex undirected weighted network. B is the explicit common vertex of the W–B–F and G1–B–G2 chains. Ordinary edges, weights, labels and vertex markers use house black.
spec.mathematics: Edges in minutes: G1–F 8, G1–B 6, G1–W 8, W–B 9, B–F 12, B–G2 8, F–G2 10, W–T 10, T–G2 6. No arrows or loops.

inlines.text: Direct walking times in minutes; – means no direct edge.

answer.worked: Use the same vertex order for rows and columns: G1, W, B, T, G2, F. Enter each direct edge weight in both corresponding cells because walking is possible in either direction. The direct connections are G1–W: 8, G1–B: 6, G1–F: 8, W–B: 9, W–T: 10, B–G2: 8, B–F: 12, T–G2: 6 and G2–F: 10, all in minutes. Put – in every remaining cell, including the diagonal, because there is no direct edge.

children.label: b
children.prompt: A tourist walks from the tree to fern gully via the waterfall and bridge.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: A faster walk that goes from the tree to fern gully is possible. Identify it.

answer.worked: T–G2–F takes $6+10=16$ minutes, which is less than 31 minutes.

children.label: c
children.prompt: A tourist undertakes the walk G1 W B F G2 B G1. How long did it take?
